reason: All three honestly report that De anima 21 and Waszink's commentary are not in the corpus, and their KG claims check out; Z is slightly more useful because it shows the candidate chapter-21 passage is actually Adv. Prax. 21 (Trinitarian, verified) and adds the Préaux and Jowers context.

Z gives the most complete and best-grounded reconstruction of the III.1 argument (opening on judgment, the phantasia/horme taxonomy, the 3.1.4 claim that the external is not the autoteles aitia) and the fullest account of Frede's view of how Origen differs from the Stoics, and it flags the lack of a Bobzien reading honestly; Y is close, with a useful point on autexousion, and X is solid but thinner.

X is the most precise comparison: it grounds Chrysippus in Cic. Fat. 41, covers Epictetus, and openly flags that the Bobzien node also describes a two-sided Chrysippean sense neutral about determinism; Y cites that same node only for the one-sided reading, and Z has rich primary sources but less nuance on the one-sided vs. two-sided debate.

All three correctly ground the IV.37 parallels (angels/humans autexousioi, no coercion, praise/blame topos) and flag the missing IV.38-39 passages, but Z alone covers the IV.38-39 nepios/agathos-teleios development with the accurate nuance that the KG credits Theophilus, not Justin, with the infant doctrine, while X omits IV.38-39 content entirely.

Z covers III.1.5-6 with the verified French Scripture passage and grounds Phil. 23.1 in both the Eusebius PE VI.11.2 Greek parallel and Amand, while Y misses the Eusebius witness and X misses III.1.6 and the content of Phil. 23.1; all three wrongly or partly overlook the Greek III.1.5 passage or omit the God-blame and Christ arguments.

Y best covers the reference claims with verified primary texts (Dial. 88.5 eleuthera proairesis, De Princ. III.1.1 just judgement and eph hemin, De Orat. 6 foreknowledge parallel) and flags its gaps honestly; Z has richer scholarship but less primary grounding, and X is solid but thinner on Justin's fate and praise-blame argument.

All three accurately reconstruct the natural/gnomic distinction and honestly flag that Bathrellos 2004 is only a name in the graph, but X adds the verified early-vs-mature development and Blowers soteriological-cost debate, Z is equally accurate with a relevant Damascene passage, while Y slightly overstates the KG (humans do not share the manner of willing vs the KG analogically) and omits the gnome concept node.

All three accurately ground Barclay 2020 nodes and honestly flag the absence of Kasemann and of Paul and the Gift 2015, but Z edges ahead by engaging Rom 9:16 directly with the verified Greek text and Origen De Princ. 3.1.18 synergist reading, giving the predestination-vs-synergism axis concrete textual footing.

Z covers the most of II.6-15 (eulabeia, the voluntary/hamartia/adikia grading from II.15.62-64, Medea/Laius, repentance after baptism in II.13) with passages that check out, Y covers II.15 more thinly, and X barely gets past II.2-4; none of them addresses the devil's autexousion, God as kakias anaitios, or proairesis/horme as the source of sin.

All three correctly reject the anti-Origenist premise and verified passages (De Autex. 8 friendship framing, PG 18.70 autexousion) support them; Z edges Y by weighing both exercise markers (dialogue, prologue, Amand hypomnema) and doctrinal stakes (theodicy, freedom as gift of obedience), while X is thinner on exercise evidence, though none explicitly develops the necessitated-elements vs human exousia contrast.

All three are accurately grounded, but Z gives the fullest account: the Stoic lexical origin, Telfer's adjective/noun distinction, Christian creation-theology uses (Justin, Theophilus, Gregory) and the Stoic-Platonist character of Origen; X adds Harl's dissent but omits Origen, and Y is solid but thinner on primary loci.

Z alone grounds the human side in VI.8.6 (virtue and intellect as masterless, near the reference claim on right reason) and accurately reports the graph's stated Patristic reception (Gregory, Ps.-Dionysius, Maximus) while flagging it as undocumented, whereas X and Y are well grounded but omit the human eph hemin analysis and assert no Patristic link despite the work node; none explicitly covers the will=ousia/no power for opposites claim.

All three accurately reproduce the KG four-step reading of Sir 15:11-20 including v.17's life-and-death choice and correctly attribute Brand, Maston and Klawans, but Z combines the bechirah framing, Brand's both-place-sin-in-human-hands point, Klawans and Maston's Romans 7 critique with an honest caveat, while Y adds a loosely supported Ezekiel link and X omits the bechirah context and Josephus detail.

All three are accurately grounded on 1QS, but X alone surfaces the KG-documented Two Ways bridge (Prigent: Barnabas 18-20 / Didache 1-6 parallel 1QS 3,13-4,26) linking the Treatise to early Christian texts, while Y offers richer Patristic contrast (massa damnata, Moon, Origen) yet, like Z, wrongly implies no 1QS-Christian link exists, and Z is thinnest on the Patristic side.

Y covers all three reference claims and grounds Alexander's richest critique (De Fato 24-25: Sophroniscus/foundation, standing/walking common cause, human as arche) in verified passages with honest caveats; Z is close and well grounded but thinner, while X barely states that the human is an arche and leans on loose KG summaries.
